subject: FinLytics: hosted quickstart & deployment-path questions
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinLytics: hosted quickstart & deployment-path questions

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we all have alignment: 

1) Primary use case and constraints
- Inference use: document summarization + embeddings for search (latency-sensitive for interactive UI).
- Data sensitivity: customer PII flows into model inputs; compliance team asked about audit logs and KMS support.
- Residency: prefer US-west, but need clarity on private VPC for regulated customers.

2) What we recommend for next phase (pilot)
- Hosted API pilot is viable for rapid onramp. It gives you sandbox endpoints, streaming for summaries, and quick access to our observability dashboard.
- If you need dedicated throughput or strict network isolation later, we can transition to Dedicated capacity or Private VPC without changing your integration code (same API surface).

3) Info we need from you to size the pilot
- Typical request profile: avg tokens per request, expected peak QPS, and % of requests that must be <=300ms.
- Which region(s) you must keep data in.
- KMS requirement (bring-your-own-key) or need to use Redwood-managed keys.

4) Proposed immediate next steps
- I attached a short Pilot Checklist (FinLytics-Pilot-Checklist.xlsx) — can you fill the traffic profile section?
- We'll provision sandbox endpoints and default trial rate caps while we review your traffic.
- Procurement: if you want a pricing sketch for Dedicated/Private, include your procurement contact and target timeline.

Attachments: FinLytics-Pilot-Checklist.xlsx, Redwood-SLA-Options.pdf

If it's helpful, I'll follow up with the quickstart details for the sandbox endpoints and the default rate/quota rules. Otherwise, let me know the best time for a 20-min follow-up later this week.

Thanks,

--
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side:

- KMS: we do have a corporate KMS and would prefer BYOK for production if that's supported. For the pilot, we can use Redwood-managed keys if BYOK adds too much friction.
- Throughput: rough target for pilot is 8k inference calls/day, with spikes up to ~150 req/s for short windows (search-heavy). Typical payload ~2k tokens; summaries average ~600 tokens.
- Audit logs: compliance wants per-request logging for 90 days and an ability to export logs to our SIEM. Is that provided with Hosted?
- Private VPC: we need a ballpark of timelines/costs for Private (on-prem or VPC) — procurement wants to know if Private is realistic within 3–4 months.

If you can provide default sandbox caps/limits and a ballpark Dedicated vs Private threshold, that will help procurement prep the internal ask.

–Liam

On Tue, Apr 11, 2028 at 10:12 AM Liam O'Connor <liam@finlytics.io> wrote:
> KMS: we do have a corporate KMS and would prefer BYOK for production if that's supported. For the pilot, we can use Redwood-managed keys if BYOK adds too much friction.
> Throughput: rough target for pilot is 8k inference calls/day, with spikes up to ~150 req/s for short windows (search-heavy). Typical payload ~2k tokens; summaries average ~600 tokens.
> Audit logs: compliance wants per-request logging for 90 days and an ability to export logs to our SIEM. Is that provided with Hosted?

Thanks — answers inline below and a recommended path: 

- BYOK and KMS: Hosted supports customer-managed keys for production (we integrate with common KMS providers). For pilot we normally use Redwood-managed keys and then flip to BYOK for prod rollouts. I will note this as part of the runbook.
- Audit logs / exports: Hosted includes request-level metadata and configurable retention. We can stream audit logs to your S3 or SIEM (via secure transfer) — standard retention tiers are 90 / 365 days. I'll loop Security for a short evidence packet (SOC2 artifact + example log schema).
- Rate caps (sandbox defaults): sandbox endpoints are provisioned with conservative defaults to avoid noisy tests: 10 rps (600 rpm) per account, 60k tokens/min token throughput cap, and 500 concurrent connections. These are adjustable as part of the pilot. For short spikes (burst windows) we allow limited bursts up to 3x the rps for up to 2 minutes via a negotiated burst policy.
- Production thresholds (rule-of-thumb): if you expect sustained >25 rps or >200k inference calls/day with low-latency SLAs, we typically recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and isolation. Private VPC/on-prem is recommended for customers with strict network isolation/regulatory constraints — timelines for Private are typically 6–12 weeks from signed order depending on environment (VPC is usually faster than on-prem).

Next immediate actions from Redwood: 
- I will provision sandbox endpoints by EOD and share creds + quickstart curl examples (streaming and embeddings).
- Sean will share SOC2 evidence and a short log-schema doc.
- Please complete the traffic-profile tab in the attached checklist; procurement: if you can share an internal timeline (target go-live and procurement window) we'll draft a ballpark pricing sketch for Dedicated vs Private.

Attachments referenced: FinLytics-Pilot-Checklist.xlsx, Redwood-SLA-Options.pdf

Let me know if you want a 20-min technical sync with our Solutions Engineer (I recommend it before we open the Dedicated sizing doc).

Thanks,

--
Monica Patel
